A request whose `query_len` exceeds `max_num_batched_tokens` is now admitted whenever the batch is empty, so the step can exceed the token budget that per-step buffers and CUDA-graph shapes are sized to.

`send` no longer raises synchronously on a broken pipe; the error is only recorded by the writer thread and surfaces on a later `put`, so callers that relied on the immediate BrokenPipe/OSError lose that signal.

bug__emberserve__f1943a4.note: suite at head: 336 passed, 0 failing, of which 0 also fail at the parent (environment or pre-existing, not evidence about this PR); 10 test(s) added

findings.message: In the tiny tensor-parallel path the shard is built and loaded but never converted to `dtype`, so its parameters stay fp32 while the KV cache and inputs use the requested dtype (e.g. fp16 in test_tp_gpu.py), which breaks or silently mismatches the forward on GPU.

`shard_tensor` always splits `lm_head.weight` by rank, but `vocab_shard` replicates the lm_head when vocab_size is not divisible by tp, so an untied checkpoint's full-vocab lm_head gets chunked and fails the shape check in `_load_tensors`.

`forward_logits_all` was not updated for the sharded lm_head, so under tensor parallelism it returns only this rank's vocab/tp logits instead of gathering them, which corrupts any caller that reads full-vocabulary logits (e.g. logit checks).

`--tensor-parallel-size` is passed into EngineConfig, but build_engine builds a full unsharded model and never calls launch_tp, so any value above 1 fails in LLMEngine.__init__ with a rank-count mismatch.
On a launch_tp failure the spawned worker processes are killed but never waited on, leaving zombie processes; the spawned worker log file handles are also never closed in spawn_workers.

findings.message: `mark_ts_utc` calls `to_timestamp` on `value`, which is a DoubleType epoch-seconds value from the `timeline.marks` map, so the cast yields null (or throws under ANSI mode) and the column is silently empty for every mark row.

`iso_ts` parses the `Z`-suffixed ISO timestamps with `to_timestamp` and no timezone, so they are interpreted in the Spark session timezone rather than UTC, shifting every ISO-format `ts_utc` when the session zone is not UTC.

The `level` expression returns null for a vLLM line with no parsable level instead of falling through to the other branches, because the nested `when` is not chained to the outer `when`, so such lines lose their level.
`args.out.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)` raises ValueError when `--out` points outside the repository, after the report has already been written, so the run fails with a traceback on the final print.

The non-stream path calls `.json()` on any 2xx body, so a non-JSON success response (for example a plain-text route like /health via the `route` shape) raises a ValueError that the `except httpx.HTTPError` does not catch, which ends the job with an unhandled exception instead of an error payload.

`{**body, "model": ...}` assumes `body` is a dict, but a caller can pass any JSON value as `body` in the `route` shape, so a list or string body raises TypeError here, which is not caught and kills the job.
For a method of GET, `json=None` is sent, so a `route` job that supplies both `method: "GET"` and a `body` silently drops the body with no error.

The `if job_input.get("openai_input")` truthiness check sends an empty `openai_input: {}` to the GET branch, which then hits the chat route with GET and returns a confusing 405 error rather than a POST.
